samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-10-29 to 2024-01-14. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In September 2023, Animal Rescue Corps (ARC) executed 'Operation September Sweep,' a multi-part rescue operation. The mission commenced on Tuesday, September 19, 2023, with the rescue of 14 dogs, primarily Labrador Retrievers that had been used for breeding and were abandoned following a divorce. Subsequently, on Saturday, September 23, 2023, ARC rescued an additional 18 dogs and puppies discovered living in a hazardous cornfield. A summary of ARC's 2023 rescues reiterated these events, noting the 14 abandoned Labradors and 18 dogs and puppies from the cornfield as part of 'Operation September Sweep' during the autumn season. [1] <2> The ninth annual "Clear the Shelters" campaign, a nationwide pet adoption and donation initiative by NBCUniversal Local, took place from August 1 to August 31, 2023. [2] The 2023 campaign resulted in more than 158,000 pets finding new homes and raised over $575,000 for participating shelters and rescues. [12, 14] An NBCUniversal Local press release on September 13, 2023, announced that the campaign had surpassed one million total adoptions since its inception in 2015. [2] More than 1,400 shelters and rescues across 49 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and Guam participated in the monthlong event. [1, 2] <3> In a significant animal hoarding case in Lake Los Angeles, California, at least 14 puppies were euthanized in early September 2023 after being rescued from a home. The Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control reported that an initial group of four puppies was brought in on September 7, 2023, and tested positive for the highly contagious parvovirus. Despite attempts to save them with fluids, antibiotics, and feedings, their condition deteriorated, leading to euthanasia. The following day, ten more puppies from the same location were brought in, but their parvovirus was so advanced that humane euthanasia was the only option. Authorities located the home and worked with a local group, Rescue Oasis, to provide care for the 24 dogs that remained on the property. The situation was described as a case of animal hoarding rather than a breeding operation or intentional cruelty. <4> A bipartisan bill, the 'Better Collaboration, Accountability, and Regulatory Enforcement for Animals Act of 2023' (S.2555), also known as the 'Better CARE for Animals Act of 2023', was introduced in the U.S. Senate and an identical companion bill was introduced in the House. [3, 4] The legislation was sponsored in the Senate by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and John Kennedy (R-LA), and in the House by Representatives Mike Quigley (D-IL) and Guy Reschenthaler (R-PA). [4] The bill aims to strengthen the Animal Welfare Act by granting the Department of Justice (DOJ) greater enforcement authority. [4] Specifically, it would allow the DOJ to seek civil penalties, pursue the revocation or suspension of licenses for violators, and facilitate the seizure and relocation of animals from licensed dealers and exhibitors suffering from mistreatment. [1, 4] The act is intended to create better collaboration between the DOJ and the U.S. Department of Agriculture to more effectively address animal abuse and unnecessary suffering for animals at research facilities, commercial breeding operations, zoos, and aquariums. [3] <5> In mid-July 2023, Animal Rescue Corps (ARC), in partnership with the BISSELL Pet Foundation and other local shelters, undertook 'Operation Skin and Bones' in Newton, Mississippi, following an urgent request from Newton County officials. [3, 5, 7] The rescue took place across two properties belonging to a self-described nonprofit, Second Paw Dog Rescue, where over 70 dogs were discovered in deplorable conditions. [3, 4, 7] The animals were suffering from severe neglect, emaciation, dehydration, and untreated injuries; many were chained to trees, and the remains of at least 15 deceased dogs were found on the properties. [3, 4, 5] The proprietors of the organization were arrested and faced charges of animal cruelty. [3, 7] The operation, one of several significant rescues ARC conducted in 2023, involved multiple partners, including Animal Rescue New Orleans (ARNO), Humane Society of South Mississippi (HSSM), and Southern Pines Animal Shelter (SPAS). [5, 6, 7] <6> In a ruling on July 5, 2023, the Wyoming Supreme Court affirmed a lower court's decision in the case of Cardenas v. Swanson, holding that damages for emotional distress cannot be recovered for the death or injury of a pet. The case arose after the three St. Bernard dogs belonging to the Cardenas family—Brooklyn, Barkley, and Jax—were caught in snares set by trapper Sigiel J. Swanson, leading to their deaths. Citing existing state law (Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 11-31-102) which defines dogs as personal property, the court declined to create a new precedent that would allow for emotional distress damages for the loss of what it legally classifies as 'animate personal property.' The court's decision reaffirmed the precedent set in Blagrove, precluding recovery for such emotional distress claims. <7> Animal Aid USA, a volunteer-based organization, conducted one of its monthly "Rescue Caravans" in June 2023. [1, 2] These regular events are central to the organization's mission of relocating animals, on average over 250 dogs a month, from high-kill shelters to a network of rescue groups where they have a greater chance of adoption. [2] The caravans transport animals that have been saved from euthanasia and given necessary veterinary care. [2] A post-event summary for the June 2023 caravan was published on the organization's website. [3, 4] <8> Animal Aid USA conducted one of its regular "Rescue Caravan" events in April 2023. These monthly caravans are a core part of the organization's mission to transport at-risk animals from overcrowded shelters to partner organizations, thereby increasing their chances of adoption. [1, 2] <9> The Animal Welfare Enforcement Improvement Act (H.R.3859) was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives on June 6, 2023, by Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) with Representative Nancy Mace (R-SC) as an original cosponsor. [2, 3, 5] The bill seeks to amend the Animal Welfare Act (AWA) to provide more robust enforcement by strengthening the licensing and oversight process for animal dealers and exhibitors, such as commercial breeders and roadside zoos. [1, 8] Key provisions include requiring annual license renewals contingent on passing an unannounced USDA inspection, denying licenses to applicants with documented humane care violations or violations of other animal protection laws, and requiring the suspension or revocation of licenses for violations that endanger animal welfare. [5, 8] The Animal Legal Defense Fund and the Animal Welfare Institute have expressed strong support for the bill, citing that it would close loopholes that allow chronic AWA violators to continue operating. [5, 8]

While the report summarized February's achievements, it also noted a successful MLK Day of Service volunteer event, which took place on January 20, 2025. <2> The Safeguard Pets, Animals, and Research Ethics (SPARE) Act, designated as H.R. 1802, was introduced in the House of Representatives. The bill was co-sponsored by Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) and Rep. Aaron Bean (R-FL). Its primary goal is to prohibit animal testing for biomedical, cosmetic, toxicity, and psychological purposes in federally funded laboratories and institutions. The legislation proposes a three-year phase-out of such testing and aims to redirect funds toward humane, scientifically advanced alternatives like organ-on-chip technology and AI-driven research. Furthermore, the SPARE Act mandates the rehabilitation and adoption or sanctuary placement for animals that were previously used in experiments. The bill includes exemptions for certain types of research, including clinical veterinary studies for the direct benefit of the animals, tasks related to service or military animals, and specific infectious disease and national security projects that are subject to annual congressional approval. <3> PetSmart Charities has officially updated its policy to permit cats positive for Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV) and Feline Leukemia Virus (FeLV) into its in-store adoption centers. This major policy revision, announced on February 26, 2025, aims to dismantle persistent, unfounded stereotypes that have previously limited the adoption opportunities for these animals. The move is celebrated by animal welfare organizations like Furkids, which notes that FIV-positive cats can live long, healthy lives and pose no significant risk of transmission to other cats in a typical home setting, as the virus primarily spreads through deep bite wounds. Prior to this nationwide rollout, PetSmart Charities had been conducting pilot programs for both FIV and FeLV positive cats in its stores. The new, inclusive policy is expected to significantly increase the chances for these often-overlooked cats to find permanent homes. <4> In February 2025, the animal rescue organization Pilots To The Rescue transported 71 dogs and 33 cats to safety. During the month, the organization also conducted two rescue missions in honor of Seuk Kim, a fellow animal rescue pilot who had passed away. A notable mission occurred on February 25, 2025, when pilot Paul Mamauag and co-pilot Mackenzie Brendlen flew an injured dog named Adelaide and 11 other dogs from Nashville, Tennessee to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The dogs had been sourced from Dallas Pets Alive! in Texas. <5> The 'Animal Cruelty Enforcement Act of 2025' (H.R. 1477) was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives on February 21, 2025. The bipartisan legislation was reintroduced by Representatives Dave Joyce (OH-14), Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06), Joe Neguse (CO-02), and Steve Cohen (TN-09). The rescued animals, which included foxes, raccoons, and wolf-dogs, were discovered living in horrific and inhumane conditions. The event will showcase a variety of food and signature drinks from some of Dallas's top chefs, with Abraham Salum serving as the Chef Chair. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In a board report on February 28, 2025, the Animal Welfare Association (AWA) detailed a successful month, having secured $12,900 in grants. This total included a notable $4,000 grant from Best Friends Animal Society aimed at improving cat transport. The report also highlighted a 44% increase in families served by their Pet Food Pantry compared to the previous year. While the report summarized February's achievements, it also noted a successful MLK Day of Service volunteer event, which took place on January 20, 2025. <2> The Safeguard Pets, Animals, and Research Ethics (SPARE) Act, designated as H.R. 1802, was introduced in the House of Representatives. The bill was co-sponsored by Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) and Rep. Aaron Bean (R-FL). Its primary goal is to prohibit animal testing for biomedical, cosmetic, toxicity, and psychological purposes in federally funded laboratories and institutions. The legislation proposes a three-year phase-out of such testing and aims to redirect funds toward humane, scientifically advanced alternatives like organ-on-chip technology and AI-driven research. Furthermore, the SPARE Act mandates the rehabilitation and adoption or sanctuary placement for animals that were previously used in experiments. The bill includes exemptions for certain types of research, including clinical veterinary studies for the direct benefit of the animals, tasks related to service or military animals, and specific infectious disease and national security projects that are subject to annual congressional approval. <3> PetSmart Charities has officially updated its policy to permit cats positive for Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV) and Feline Leukemia Virus (FeLV) into its in-store adoption centers. This major policy revision, announced on February 26, 2025, aims to dismantle persistent, unfounded stereotypes that have previously limited the adoption opportunities for these animals. The move is celebrated by animal welfare organizations like Furkids, which notes that FIV-positive cats can live long, healthy lives and pose no significant risk of transmission to other cats in a typical home setting, as the virus primarily spreads through deep bite wounds. Prior to this nationwide rollout, PetSmart Charities had been conducting pilot programs for both FIV and FeLV positive cats in its stores. The new, inclusive policy is expected to significantly increase the chances for these often-overlooked cats to find permanent homes. <4> In February 2025, the animal rescue organization Pilots To The Rescue transported 71 dogs and 33 cats to safety. During the month, the organization also conducted two rescue missions in honor of Seuk Kim, a fellow animal rescue pilot who had passed away. A notable mission occurred on February 25, 2025, when pilot Paul Mamauag and co-pilot Mackenzie Brendlen flew an injured dog named Adelaide and 11 other dogs from Nashville, Tennessee to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The dogs had been sourced from Dallas Pets Alive! in Texas. <5> The 'Animal Cruelty Enforcement Act of 2025' (H.R. 1477) was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives on February 21, 2025. The bipartisan legislation was reintroduced by Representatives Dave Joyce (OH-14), Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06), Joe Neguse (CO-02), and Steve Cohen (TN-09). The bill proposes the establishment of a dedicated Animal Cruelty Crimes Section within the Department of Justice's Environment and Natural Resources Division. This section would be tasked with aiding the investigation, enforcement, and prosecution of federal animal cruelty crimes to ensure these laws are effectively enforced. <6> In a significant rescue operation in Ashtabula County, northeastern Ohio, authorities and the Human World for Animals confiscated over 250 wild animals from a fur and urine farm on January 18, 2025. The rescued animals, which included foxes, raccoons, and wolf-dogs, were discovered living in horrific and inhumane conditions. Investigators found that many animals were suffering from missing limbs, ears, tails, and toes, likely as a result of the wire flooring of their cages and steel-jaw traps scattered around the property. <7> The SPCA of Texas will host its premier food-focused fundraising event, Paws Cause 2025, on May 22, 2025, at the Dallas Animal Care Center. This elegant, cocktail-hour gathering aims to raise funds for the organization's crucial lifesaving outreach programs, which support animals both in and out of shelters and assist in keeping pets with their families. The event will showcase a variety of food and signature drinks from some of Dallas's top chefs, with Abraham Salum serving as the Chef Chair. All proceeds from the evening will directly benefit the SPCA of Texas's mission to provide exceptional care and find loving homes for animals.

The bill was introduced in the Senate (S.1538) by Senators John Kennedy (R-LA) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), with a companion bill introduced in the House of Representatives by Representatives Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY), Mike Quigley (D-IL), Guy Reschenthaler (R-PA), and Sharice Davids (D-KS). The primary goal of the act is to strengthen the U.S. Department of Justice's (DOJ) ability to enforce the AWA by granting it authority comparable to that of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), including the ability to seek license suspensions and revocations, pursue civil penalties, and seize animals from abusive situations. It would also mandate a memorandum of understanding between the USDA and DOJ to facilitate better collaboration and evidence sharing to address chronic and severe violations at facilities like commercial breeding operations (puppy mills), research labs, and roadside zoos. Supporting organizations, such as the Humane World Action Fund, emphasize that the bill provides necessary tools to hold violators accountable where enforcement has historically been lacking. <2> In April 2025, the non-profit organization Pilots To The Rescue transported 67 animals to safety. Additionally, the organization transported 6 foxes, 2 skunks, and a coyote from an illegal fur and urine farm in Ohio.
